info.title: VideTrack API
info.description: Token-authenticated REST surface of a VideTrack instance. Create a token in Settings → API; send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A token carries `read` and optionally `write`. Answers are camelCase under `data` (with `meta` where there is something to count or page); a position carries the user's state as `state`, and a write that changes a position adds `states`: every state it touched, keyed `type:ref`. Request fields are snake_case.

get.summary:
The user's own lists, system ones first — the same order the lists
page shows, without the poster collage a JSON client has no use for

patch.summary:
The system watchlist keeps its identity — only its visibility moves.
The action enforces that; the endpoint does not have to know

put.summary: The user's own lists in the order given; the watchlist keeps the lead, foreign ids are ignored

post.summary: A viewable list copied into the caller's own, items and order with it

put.summary: A list's positions in the order given, numbered 1..n; ids of other lists are ignored

The bell exception on a title: `follow` forces release tracking, `mute`
silences it, null hands the title back to the tracking matrix

Two semantics behind one field: `dropped` closes the current attempt,
`on_hold` pauses the open one, null clears both — on a season, the
show's inherited one included. Clearing resumes the attempt with the
sessions logged before the pause; `discard_progress` throws it away

get.summary:
The user's notification feed, newest first: each one worded in the
language of the request, the raw event data beside it for a client that
words its own
Every viewing / playthrough of the position, newest first

post.summary:
Logs a completion. On a container this settles every unwatched aired
descendant, so `meta.created` says how many entries that turned out
to be. With `next_episode` the play lands on the one episode the
container stands at instead — which one is a server question

delete.summary:
Unmarks the whole position — every entry of the active cycle, down the
hierarchy. Deleting one viewing is DELETE /plays/{play}

patch.summary:
Corrects the recorded cost of one play (games: post-game content played
after completing). Answers with the play and the states it moved

delete.summary:
Removes one viewing from the history, not the whole position. The
play is gone, so the answer is the position it belonged to

get.summary:
The top of the statistics page: the time the period took, its counts
per type, how its titles were rated and what became of them, its first
and last finished title

One section of the statistics page: `activity` (when things were
finished), `taste` (where the time went, release years, genres,
lengths), `origins` (countries, languages, networks or studios),
`creators` (cast, directors, writers, authors), `ratings` (against
everyone else's) or `records` (streak, busiest day, marathon); `summary`
is the top, the same as the statistics without a section
The kinds that have something for the user, with how much waits behind each

MediaRequest.description:
A call addressed to one position: `media/{type}/{ref}`. The route holds the
ref's shape; this adds its length and turns a type the instance does not
serve (unknown, or a module whose keys are not configured) into a resource
that does not exist — 404, not an error on a field the client never sent.

Used as is where the target is all there is (reading, unmarking, clearing a
rating); the writes that take fields extend it. Timestamp fields share the
'now' | 'release' | explicit-date convention of logging a play.
MediaRequest.title: MediaRequest

watched_at.description:
'now' | 'release' (each play stamped with the item's own
release date) | explicit date, optionally with time, not in
the future.

amount.description:
Real cost of the completion in the type's progress unit
(games: minutes played); ignored for types without one.

new_attempt.description:
Keep a latest dropped attempt as its own history entry instead
of completing it in place (games: separate playthroughs).

merge_hours.description:
When replacing a dropped attempt without an explicit total:
add its frozen hours to the sessions, or start fresh.

next_episode.description:
Containers only: mark the one episode the container stands at
instead of the whole run. Which episode that is gets resolved
server-side — the client knows the show it clicked, not its tree.

UpdateFollowRequest.description:
The bell on a title. It lives on hierarchy roots alone: season and episode
events roll up to the show, so subscribing lower means nothing.

anyOf.description: null clears the exception — the tracking matrix decides again.

UpdateFollowRequest.title: UpdateFollowRequest

title.description:
The watchlist has no title to send: it is named in the
reader's language, and only its visibility changes.

UpdateMediaStatusRequest.description:
One endpoint, two attempt-model semantics: `dropped` CLOSES the current
attempt (a dated play entry — allowed on roots with a user status and on
nested positions, where it reads as "skip"), while `on_hold` pauses the
OPEN attempt (state row, roots only). Null clears both: the open state
and a current drop. "Playing" (in_progress) is automatic — sessions set
it (LogProgress); it is never written here.

amount.description:
Hours sunk into the dropped attempt (progress types) — the
drop freezes them into the play entry.

dropped_at.description:
The drop is a dated history entry — same 'now' | 'release' |
explicit date convention as logging a play.

discard_progress.description:
Clearing the status resumes the attempt by default; this asks
to throw it away instead, logged sessions included.

UpdateMediaStatusRequest.title: UpdateMediaStatusRequest

UpdatePlayAmountRequest.description:
Corrects the recorded cost of one play (games: minutes of that
playthrough). Null clears it; zero is not a cost, so it is refused rather
than quietly read as "clear".
UpdatePlayAmountRequest.title: UpdatePlayAmountRequest

add.description:
One of the two: `add` appends a session, `set` overwrites the
counter (progress editor). Units come from the type registry.

WatchCyclesRequest.description:
Viewing cycles belong to a root with a hierarchy under it (a show): only
there does "start again from the first episode" mean anything.
WatchCyclesRequest.title: WatchCyclesRequest
